notes:
Anivora 0.1.46 improves large anime catalogs and provider chapter loading, restores keyboard-visible comment filters, and adds portable full-app ZIP backups with selective merge and interrupted-restore recovery.

- Virtualized episode cards, indexed download selection, stable catalog caches, and bounded manga provider requests reduce unnecessary work on large titles.
- Info-page hero framing, rounded sheets, focused pulsing skeletons, and category spacing are corrected. Portrait and landscape player controls remain intact.
- Application dialogs share Anivora styling and transparent backdrops, with protected asynchronous actions.
- Full backups separate library, watch/read progress, preferences, player settings, subtitles, notification history, and recent searches. Restore validates every file before mutation, preserves newer local progress, and uses a recovery journal. Credentials, downloaded media/jobs, device folder permissions, and Android permission grants are excluded.
- MAL ZIP exports contain Anime_List.xml, Manga_List.xml, and supplementary Anivora title identities, including titles without verified MAL IDs. Legacy list JSON and URL text exports remain available.
- A verified update now shows Install Update, including after installer cancellation or app restart. Missing/corrupt files are rejected. Native transfers accept unknown response lengths while enforcing the release size/checksum, validate resumed ranges, and renew GitHub redirects on retry.
- The owner dashboard adds server-enforced ten-minute inactivity, server-side logout revocation, browser Back confirmation, origin-specific AniList checks and a direct device test. Render monitoring preserves reported bandwidth units and does not invent a monthly billing balance.

Package: com.brandon300.anivora. Android version code: 48. ARM64 release with the existing signing certificate; intended to update existing Anivora installations without removing their data.

- The redesigned owner dashboard is dark (charcoal/navy with indigo accents). The original dark login page is restored. The Render meter shows approximate recorded usage against the configured 5 GB allowance; retained samples do not establish a complete monthly billing balance.

Source commit: https://github.com/brandon-300/Anivora/commit/d11dea8516b249aa460b7cfa17e577d4d3603ba7

APK SHA-256: `867b99d760d695c3a0131ab0b5ad0d30d5af77dfc30d1964efcb6b9e1d7b0ce8`

Verified locally: signed non-debuggable ARM64 release; original package/signing certificate; packaged source/bundle match; 70 native release unit tests; TypeScript; lint; 397 application tests; 18 Expo Doctor checks; Expo dependency compatibility; 206 Discord tests; 43 support-site tests.

Android 14 emulator evidence on identical application inputs: all 29 native integration tests passed at d2e413038e684b458d78545fa6adace88aa03845; all ten portrait/landscape/player UI checks, a separate landscape comments/keyboard scenario, and all six updater scenarios passed at deaeeadf6ae0b695deffb5281d28f5872afa6ab9. Updater tests exercised real interruption/range resume, main-process death with independent background completion, installer cancellation without redownload, missing/corrupt APK recovery, and an actual signed debug package upgrade preserving data. Debug test APKs are not distributed.

Build limitation: GitHub account billing prevented the final hosted workflow from starting. This release was built and independently verified locally. The final commit changes only a test wait for asynchronous notification publication; that modified instrumentation test was not rerun. No claim is made that the final hosted workflow passed.

Physical Infinix Hot 50i/XOS and physical Cast playback were not tested. Provider availability depends on the upstream service/network; WeebCentral catalog access was blocked from the test environment, although known Chainsaw Man Chapter 1 pages decoded. That chapter’s black-and-white artwork is upstream content and was left unchanged.
